I couldn't say much more than that without thinking about it more."

We want to understand what you meant by "there was something near the bottom of one of the screens, some kind of action I think, though I couldn't quite tell what it was for", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The large "Continue Shopping" button located in the lower section of the layout.
B) The "Place Order" button positioned directly below the primary action area.
C) The legal disclaimer and policy links located at the very bottom of the page.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
turns.a: If I had to pick... probably B? I think. Though I'm not sure that's exactly it — it might be closer to another option, depending on how you're defining it. It's more of a general feeling than a specific thing. Other people might not even notice.

turns.q: What kind of work situation or real-world scenario typically brings you to a screen like this?
turns.a: I'm not sure I have one specific moment in mind. It's more of a... recurring thing, I suppose. When the team needs to process something quickly and there's not much time for setup. Though I'm not sure that's specific enough.

turns.q: What specific information were you hoping to confirm about the order process when looking at the placement of that "Place Order" button?
turns.a: I suppose just... complete the transaction. Get it submitted. I don't usually think of it as a 'job' — it's more like a step in something larger. Someone else usually handles the follow-up.

turns.q: What specific improvement to the "Place Order" button's placement would make this layout feel successful for your needs?
turns.a: I think the improvement will if the confirmation appeared and transition is prominent. That's what success looks like for this kind of thing.

turns.q: What is it about the button's appearance—specifically its fill, color, or border—that makes it hard to identify as the primary action?
turns.a: I mean... it was just a small thing. The button wasn't as prominent as I expected. Most of the time I'd figure it out. It's not a blocker, exactly.

turns.q: Is the issue that the button has no fill—making it look like an outline-only style—or is it that the color of the button is too similar to the background?
turns.a: Well I would say almost all of them. The problem is visibility, really. The button to submit — the 'Place Order' button — didn't look like a primary action. It looked like a label. So I spent time looking for something that was already there, just... not visible enough.

turns.q: When you look at the "Place Order" button, what specific visual property—such as its fill, color, or border style—makes it blend into the background rather than standing out?
turns.a: I would say all making it invisible
